rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable incarcerated/strangulated inguinal hernia (both rules)
rule_level_problems.problem: 'No stools ... for past 24 hours' is encoded via onset of 'Constipation' >= 24 h; Constipation (a common symptom) is not equivalent to no stool passed in 24 h, so a chronically constipated patient with a reducible hernia, cough impulse and inability to pass wind would be labelled incarcerated AND strangulated and triaged Urgent, while the intended 'no stools' meaning has no direct concept.

rule_level_problems.rule: Inguinal hernia rules (probable inguinal, incarcerated, strangulated) and lymphadenopathy negation
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Gets bigger when standing/coughing/passing stool' is represented only by 'Cough impulse of mass present'. A groin hernia noticed only on standing/straining fails every hernia rule, and (because the negation also uses only cough impulse) is instead labelled probable lymphadenopathy, and the Urgent hernia priority cannot fire.

The two probable rules have identical evidence, so every qualifying patient gets both diagnoses; this matches the page's 'incarcerated/strangulated' but the system cannot distinguish them. Acceptable, but worth noting.

Hot/tender groin node -> bubo, TB-suggestive symptoms -> aspirate for TB, and the drug-hypersensitivity medication list are not encoded as possible diagnoses; the localised/generalised split is not used anywhere.
Contact time window (21 days before symptom onset) and 'unexplained' rash qualifier dropped; Body temperature criterion is fine as a routine vital.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully in structure (Urgent priority anchored on Groin mass, probable incarcerated/strangulated hernia and aneurysm rules), but the hernia criterion 'gets bigger when standing/coughing/passing stool' is reduced to a cough impulse and 'no stools for 24 h' is approximated by Constipation onset, both of which affect who is triaged Urgent and who is mislabelled lymphadenopathy. Thyroid, hidradenitis, lymphadenopathy and mpox rules are largely correct; the flowchart's bubo, TB-suspicion and drug-hypersensitivity branches are not encoded.
